# opencode-gentle-ai-updater

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin that tells you when **Gentle AI** has
updates — and applies them for you. It checks in the background on startup
(throttled to once every 6 hours), shows a toast when something is behind, and
upgrades on demand via a tool or the `/gentle-update` command.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> OpenCode cannot restart itself from a plugin. After an upgrade you must
> restart OpenCode **manually** — the plugin tells you when. See
> [Restart required](#restart-required).

## Quick start

1. Install the plugin — [from npm](#from-npm) or [from a local file](#from-local-files).
2. Install the [`/gentle-update` command](#the-gentle-update-command).
3. **Restart OpenCode.**
4. Run `/gentle-update`, or ask the agent to run the `gentle_ai_check_updates` tool.

> Requires the **`gentle-ai` binary on your PATH**. Without it the plugin is a
> silent no-op (no toast, no error).

## What it does

- **Startup check** — runs `gentle-ai update` at most once every 6h (cached at
  `~/.gentle-ai/cache/update-check.json`) and toasts you if any managed tool is
  behind.
- **`gentle_ai_check_updates`** tool — re-runs the check on demand and reports
  `installed → latest` per tool. Read-only.
- **`gentle_ai_upgrade`** tool — runs `gentle-ai upgrade`, then `gentle-ai sync`
  (when `sync: true`, the default) to apply config/skill changes.
- **Remote variant (opt-in, off by default)** — if you run Gentle AI / Engram on
  a remote host over SSH, enable it to also check and upgrade the remote and
  reconnect the local tunnel. See [Remote variant](#remote-variant-built-in-opt-in).
- **TUI status indicator (optional)** — a small SolidJS TUI plugin that shows the
  pending-update count in the **session sidebar** and on the **home/splash
  screen**. See [TUI status indicator](#tui-status-indicator).
- **Silent when irrelevant** — if `gentle-ai` is not on PATH, it does nothing.

## Requirements

- The **`gentle-ai` binary** on your PATH.
- OpenCode **`>= 1.17.0`** (peer dependency on `@opencode-ai/plugin`).

## Install

Pick **one** method.

### From npm

Published on npm: [opencode-gentle-ai-updater](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-gentle-ai-updater).

Add it to the `plugin` array in your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["opencode-gentle-ai-updater"]
}
```

OpenCode installs and caches the package automatically on the next startup.

### From local files

Works today, without npm. Build the bundle and drop it into your global plugin
directory:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bvironn/opencode-gentle-ai-updater.git
cd opencode-gentle-ai-updater
bun install            # the "prepare" script builds dist/
cp dist/index.js ~/.config/opencode/plugins/gentle-ai-updater.js
```

OpenCode auto-loads any `.js`/`.ts` file in `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` at
startup — no `opencode.json` change needed.

> [!NOTE]
> The local file imports `@opencode-ai/plugin` at runtime. Gentle AI setups
> already provide it. On a vanilla OpenCode config, add it to your config's
> `package.json` (`~/.config/opencode/package.json`) so OpenCode can resolve it.

## The `/gentle-update` command

npm plugins **cannot** auto-install command files, so this step is always
manual. Copy the shipped command into your commands directory:

```bash
cp commands/gentle-update.md ~/.config/opencode/commands/gentle-update.md
```

After a restart, `/gentle-update` walks you through checking and — with your
confirmation — applying updates.

## Tools

| Tool | Arguments | What it does |
|------|-----------|--------------|
| `gentle_ai_check_updates` | none | Runs `gentle-ai update` (and `ssh <host> gentle-ai update` when remote is enabled), refreshes the cache, returns a summary of pending updates. Read-only. |
| `gentle_ai_upgrade` | `sync: boolean` (default `true`), `target: "local" \| "remote" \| "all"` (default `"local"`) | Runs `gentle-ai upgrade`; when `sync` is true, also runs `gentle-ai sync`. With `target` `remote`/`all`, also upgrades the remote host and reconnects the local tunnel. |

## Remote variant (built-in, opt-in)

Some setups run **Gentle AI and Engram on a remote host over SSH** (for example,
Engram persisting to a shared box) with a local SSH tunnel forwarding to it. The
remote feature is **built into this plugin** — there is no separate branch or
package. It is **off by default**: the plugin behaves local-only until you enable
remote in configuration.

When enabled, the plugin:

- also runs `ssh <host> gentle-ai update` on startup and folds remote-pending
  tools into the same toast (labeled with the host);
- exposes `target: "remote" | "all"` on `gentle_ai_upgrade`, which upgrades
  Gentle AI + Engram on the remote, restarts the remote Engram, and restarts the
  **local** tunnel service to reconnect.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The remote path targets **only** `gentle-ai` and `engram`. It never touches
> other services (e.g. nginx, docker, the firewall) on the remote host.

### Configuration (config file + env vars)

Remote behavior is configured from **two sources**, resolved **per field** with
this precedence:

> **environment variable** (if set) → **config file** value (if present) →
> **built-in default**

The env var wins for its own field; an unset env var falls back to the file; a
missing/malformed file falls back to the built-in default. The config loader
**never throws** — a missing or broken file is the same as "use defaults".

**Config file** — `~/.config/opencode/gentle-ai-update.json`:

```json
{
  "remote": {
    "enabled": false,
    "host": "core",
    "engramRestartCmd": "",
    "localTunnelService": "engram-tunnel.service",
    "localRestartPrefix": ""
  }
}
```

**Field reference** (file key → env override → default):

| Field (`remote.*`) | Env override | Default | Purpose |
|--------------------|--------------|---------|---------|
| `enabled` | `GENTLE_REMOTE_ENABLED` | `false` | Master switch for the remote path. Truthy env values: `1`, `true`, `yes`, `on`. |
| `host` | `GENTLE_REMOTE_HOST` | `core` | SSH host/alias to reach the remote. |
| `engramRestartCmd` | `GENTLE_REMOTE_ENGRAM_RESTART_CMD` | `""` (→ `systemctl restart engram`) | Command run via `ssh <host> <cmd>` to restart Engram on the remote. Set this when Engram is not a plain systemd unit. |
| `localTunnelService` | `GENTLE_LOCAL_TUNNEL_SERVICE` | `engram-tunnel.service` | Local systemd unit restarted to reconnect the tunnel after a remote upgrade. |
| `localRestartPrefix` | `GENTLE_LOCAL_RESTART_PREFIX` | `""` | Optional privilege prefix (e.g. `sudo`) for the local tunnel restart. |

Minimal opt-in via the config file:

```json
{ "remote": { "enabled": true, "host": "core" } }
```

Or via env (overrides the file per field):

```bash
export GENTLE_REMOTE_ENABLED=1
export GENTLE_REMOTE_HOST=core
```

## TUI status indicator

An optional SolidJS **TUI plugin** (`tui/index.tsx`) renders a compact
`Gentle AI · N updates` line by reading the same
`~/.gentle-ai/cache/update-check.json` cache.

It **always** shows in the **session sidebar** (host slot `sidebar_content`). Its
**home/splash-screen** behavior is chosen by the `tui.animatedIntro` flag:

| `tui.animatedIntro` | Home screen |
|---------------------|-------------|
| `false` (default) | a plain `Gentle AI · N updates` line next to the Tip (`home_bottom`); the logo is left alone. |
| `true` | an **animated** Gentle AI rose that reveals line-by-line, then fades in the update summary (`home_logo`) — this **replaces** the static logo. |

Set it in `~/.config/opencode/gentle-ai-update.json` (env
`GENTLE_TUI_ANIMATED_INTRO` overrides):

```json
{ "tui": { "animatedIntro": true } }
```

### Install

TUI plugins are registered in `tui.json`, separate from server plugins:

```bash
# Copy the indicator into your TUI plugins directory
cp tui/index.tsx ~/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/gentle-ai-update-status.tsx
```

Then add its absolute path to the `plugin` array in `~/.config/opencode/tui.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/tui.json",
  "plugin": [
    "/root/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/gentle-ai-update-status.tsx"
  ]
}
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> If you enable `animatedIntro`, remove any logo plugin that owns the `home_logo`
> slot (e.g. `gentle-logo`) from `tui.json` — both register `home_logo` (mode
> `replace`). Note `gentle-ai sync` manages `gentle-logo` and may re-add it; if it
> does, remove it again.

Restart OpenCode. The status line appears on the home screen immediately and in
the sidebar once you open a session. It refreshes from the cache every 30s.

## Restart required

OpenCode loads configs, skills, and plugins **only at startup**, and a plugin
**cannot restart OpenCode**. So after running `gentle_ai_upgrade` (or
`/gentle-update`), you must **restart OpenCode manually** for the new
configs/plugins to take effect. The plugin never attempts an auto-restart — it
just reminds you.

## Scope

**Local by default.** Out of the box the plugin operates only on the `gentle-ai`
binary on the **current machine's PATH** and performs no SSH or remote
operations. The [remote variant](#remote-variant-built-in-opt-in) is opt-in; when
enabled it adds SSH checks/upgrades scoped strictly to `gentle-ai` and `engram`.

description: Check for and apply pending Gentle AI updates
---

You are helping the user keep their Gentle AI tooling up to date.

TASK:

1. Call the `gentle_ai_check_updates` tool. This runs `gentle-ai update` and reports which managed tools have updates available (installed → latest).
2. Report the result to the user in a short, clear summary:
   - If nothing is pending, say everything is up to date and STOP.
   - If updates are pending, list each tool with its installed → latest version.
3. If updates are pending, ASK the user whether they want to apply them now. STOP and wait for their answer. Do not upgrade without explicit confirmation.
4. If the user confirms, call the `gentle_ai_upgrade` tool (leave `sync` at its default of `true` so agent configs and skills are updated after the binary upgrade).
5. After the upgrade completes, remind the user clearly:
   - OpenCode CANNOT be restarted from within a plugin.
   - They MUST restart OpenCode manually for the new configs, skills, and plugins to take effect.

RULES:

- If `gentle-ai` is not installed, the tools will say so. Relay that and STOP.
- Never promise an automatic restart. The restart is always manual.
- Keep your messages concise.
